findings.trigger_condition: The stream contains equal node values where one value is hashable and the other is unhashable, for example an unhashable class U with __eq__ returning True for 1, and edges [(1, 0), (U(), 0)].
findings.root_cause: Hashable values are searched only in hash_buckets, while unhashable values are searched only in unhashable_nodes. The registry never compares a hashable candidate against previously stored unhashable values or vice versa, so equal values can receive different node IDs.
findings.impact: Equal node values are not deduplicated as required. The example should represent the same edge twice and produce [[0], [1]], but the implementation creates a third node and produces separate incorrect layering such as [[1], [0], [U()]]. It can also produce incorrect cycle detection and .nodes contents.
findings.suggested_validation: Define class U with __hash__ = None and __eq__(self, other): return other == 1. Run dependency_layers([(1, 0), (U(), 0)]). Expected: two logical nodes, layers [[0], [1]]; actual: three IDs and layers [[1], [0], [U()]] (with the first stored object for each ID).

confirmation.evidence: reproduced: dependency_layers([(1,0),(U(),0)]) -> 3 logical nodes [[0],[1,U]]; matches supplemental check cross_hashability FAIL for subtest_12 in replay-v2

findings.trigger_condition: The input contains N distinct unhashable node values, such as a one-shot generator yielding ([i+1], [i]) for i in range(N).
findings.root_cause: Every unhashable lookup linearly scans all previously registered unhashable nodes. Thus registering or looking up each of N unique unhashable values costs O(N) equality checks, making the full identity registry O(N^2) in the number of nodes (in addition to the cost of equality itself).
findings.impact: Large valid graphs with unhashable nodes can require quadratic time and become impractical or time out, violating the requirement to handle inputs without unreasonable asymptotic resource use.
findings.suggested_validation: Benchmark dependency_layers(([i+1], [i]) for i in range(N)) with increasing N, using fresh one-element lists. Expected scalable near-linear graph processing; actual registry work grows quadratically because each new list scans the accumulated unhashable_nodes list.

confirmation.evidence: unhashable-deps probe: t(1500)=0.0469s, t(3000)=0.1961s, ratio 4.18x on 2x input => quadratic; not covered by hidden evaluator (its 50k checks use hashable nodes)
